lines.text: Number the pages of a book, and count every digit you print.
lines.caption: Number the pages of a book, and count every digit you print.

lines.text: Here's a surprise. Ninety-nine pages use one hundred eighty-nine digits, not twice ninety-nine.
lines.caption: Here's a surprise. Ninety-nine pages use one hundred eighty-nine digits, not twice ninety-nine.

lines.text: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's find out why, and crack today's puzzle.
lines.caption: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's find out why, and crack today's puzzle.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: The pages of a book are numbered in order, starting at page one.
lines.caption: The pages of a book are numbered in order, starting at page one.

lines.text: The total number of digits printed is exactly twice the number of pages.
lines.caption: The total number of digits printed is exactly twice the number of pages.

lines.text: How many pages does the book have? Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: How many pages does the book have? Here are the five choices.

lines.text: Let's break it down. Page seven uses one digit.
lines.caption: Let's break it down. Page seven uses one digit.

lines.text: Page forty-two uses two digits. Page one hundred five uses three digits.
lines.caption: Page forty-two uses two digits. Page one hundred five uses three digits.

lines.text: Take a small book with twelve pages. Nine pages with one digit, then three pages with two.
lines.caption: Take a small book with twelve pages. Nine pages with one digit, then three pages with two.

lines.text: That's fifteen digits. Twice twelve is twenty-four, so fifteen digits is too few.
lines.caption: That's fifteen digits. Twice twelve is twenty-four, so fifteen digits is too few.

lines.text: We want a book where the digits equal two times the pages, exactly.
lines.caption: We want a book where the digits equal two times the pages, exactly.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's count the digits in groups.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's count the digits in groups.

lines.text: Pages one to nine are nine pages with one digit each. That's nine digits.
lines.caption: Pages one to nine are nine pages with one digit each. That's nine digits.

lines.text: Pages ten to ninety-nine are ninety pages with two digits each: one hundred eighty digits.
lines.caption: Pages ten to ninety-nine are ninety pages with two digits each: one hundred eighty digits.

lines.text: So a book of ninety-nine pages uses one hundred eighty-nine digits.
lines.caption: So a book of ninety-nine pages uses one hundred eighty-nine digits.

lines.text: But our target, twice the pages, is one hundred ninety-eight. We're nine digits short.
lines.caption: But our target, twice the pages, is one hundred ninety-eight. We're nine digits short.

lines.text: Each two-digit page adds two digits, and our target grows by two. The gap never closes.
lines.caption: Each two-digit page adds two digits, and our target grows by two. The gap never closes.

lines.text: So no book under one hundred pages works. We need some three-digit pages.
lines.caption: So no book under one hundred pages works. We need some three-digit pages.

lines.text: Page one hundred adds three digits, but the target only grows by two.
lines.caption: Page one hundred adds three digits, but the target only grows by two.

lines.text: So the gap shrinks from nine digits to eight digits.
lines.caption: So the gap shrinks from nine digits to eight digits.

lines.text: Every three-digit page closes the gap by one more digit.
lines.caption: Every three-digit page closes the gap by one more digit.

lines.text: After nine three-digit pages, the gap is zero! That's page one hundred eight.
lines.caption: After nine three-digit pages, the gap is zero! That's page one hundred eight.

lines.text: Let's check. Nine, plus one hundred eighty, plus twenty-seven, is two hundred sixteen digits.
lines.caption: Let's check. Nine, plus one hundred eighty, plus twenty-seven, is two hundred sixteen digits.

lines.text: And twice one hundred eight is two hundred sixteen. It matches! That's Choice C.
lines.caption: And twice one hundred eight is two hundred sixteen. It matches! That's Choice C.

lines.text: Here's a faster way. Pretend every page owes exactly two digits.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way. Pretend every page owes exactly two digits.

lines.text: A one-digit page pays only one. So each one is one digit short.
lines.caption: A one-digit page pays only one. So each one is one digit short.

lines.text: Nine one-digit pages leave us nine digits short.
lines.caption: Nine one-digit pages leave us nine digits short.

lines.text: A two-digit page pays exactly two. Those pages are perfectly even.
lines.caption: A two-digit page pays exactly two. Those pages are perfectly even.

lines.text: A three-digit page pays three, so each one gives one extra digit.
lines.caption: A three-digit page pays three, so each one gives one extra digit.

lines.text: To cancel nine missing digits, we need nine three-digit pages: page one hundred to one hundred eight.
lines.caption: To cancel nine missing digits, we need nine three-digit pages: page one hundred to one hundred eight.

lines.text: After that, every new page adds an extra digit, so we can never balance again.
lines.caption: After that, every new page adds an extra digit, so we can never balance again.

lines.text: So one hundred eight pages is the only answer!
lines.caption: So one hundred eight pages is the only answer!

lines.text: So when would you pick each way? Counting in groups gives you the totals to check.
lines.caption: So when would you pick each way? Counting in groups gives you the totals to check.

lines.text: The balance trick is faster, because it skips all the big sums.
lines.caption: The balance trick is faster, because it skips all the big sums.

lines.text: Choice A, ninety-nine pages, forgets that pages one to nine have one digit. It's nine digits short.
lines.caption: Choice A, ninety-nine pages, forgets that pages one to nine have one digit. It's nine digits short.

lines.text: Choice B, one hundred pages, is a nice round guess. It's still eight digits short.
lines.caption: Choice B, one hundred pages, is a nice round guess. It's still eight digits short.

lines.text: Choice D, one hundred seventeen pages, goes too far. It uses two hundred forty-three digits.
lines.caption: Choice D, one hundred seventeen pages, goes too far. It uses two hundred forty-three digits.

lines.text: But twice the pages is only two hundred thirty-four. That's nine digits too many.
lines.caption: But twice the pages is only two hundred thirty-four. That's nine digits too many.

lines.text: Choice E is one hundred eighty-nine. That counts digits, not pages!
lines.caption: Choice E is one hundred eighty-nine. That counts digits, not pages!

lines.text: So here's a great habit: count the digits for your answer, and check it.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit: count the digits for your answer, and check it.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now the digits are exactly THREE times the number of pages.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now the digits are exactly THREE times the number of pages.

lines.text: How many pages does that book have?
lines.caption: How many pages does that book have?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's use the balance trick again. This time, each page owes three digits.
lines.caption: Let's use the balance trick again. This time, each page owes three digits.

lines.text: Each one-digit page is two digits short. Nine pages make eighteen digits short.
lines.caption: Each one-digit page is two digits short. Nine pages make eighteen digits short.

lines.text: Each two-digit page is one digit short. Ninety pages make ninety digits short.
lines.caption: Each two-digit page is one digit short. Ninety pages make ninety digits short.

lines.text: Add them up. Eighteen plus ninety gives one hundred eight missing digits.
lines.caption: Add them up. Eighteen plus ninety gives one hundred eight missing digits.

lines.text: Three-digit pages are even. Each four-digit page gives one extra digit.
lines.caption: Three-digit pages are even. Each four-digit page gives one extra digit.

lines.text: So we need one hundred eight four-digit pages: from one thousand to one thousand one hundred seven!
lines.caption: So we need one hundred eight four-digit pages: from one thousand to one thousand one hundred seven!

lines.text: If you found one thousand one hundred seven pages, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found one thousand one hundred seven pages, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Count the digits in groups: one-digit pages, then two-digit pages, then three-digit pages.
lines.caption: Count the digits in groups: one-digit pages, then two-digit pages, then three-digit pages.

lines.text: Then track the gap to the target, and find where it hits zero.
lines.caption: Then track the gap to the target, and find where it hits zero.
